text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 1.5% over two weeks and dipped slightly today, driven by a sharp selloff earlier this week that wiped out $41 per share in four days (November 13–18). The trigger appears to be deteriorating crude oil prices: US oil dropped from above $100 per barrel in early November to $89.53 today, compressing refining margins—the profit a refiner makes by turning crude into gasoline and diesel. Refineries are still running near capacity at 95.7%, but lower crude prices and steady fuel inventories (gasoline and diesel storage both ample) mean less room to make money on each barrel processed.

The broader energy sector is in flux: Middle Eastern tensions are simmering rather than escalating (Saudi Arabia and Iran both signaling some openness to negotiation), so geopolitical risk to oil supply is muted for now. Meanwhile, long-term structural headwinds loom—data center electricity demand could double by 2030, potentially shifting investment away from traditional energy infrastructure, and new permitting reforms may ease deployment of renewable alternatives.
